name: Guatemala's confrontation with Barrio 18 and MS-13
started: 2026-01-17 (Barrio 18 prison riots and coordinated killings of police)
summary: In January 2026 Barrio 18 members took 46 hostages in three prisons and killed police officers in and around Guatemala City, prompting a 30-day nationwide state of siege. By late July 2026, 20 police officers had been killed on duty that year, double the total for 2025, half of them in gang attacks.

background: Guatemala's Barrio 18 and MS-13 gangs run extortion and contract-killing rackets from inside prisons. The US and Guatemala classify both as terrorist organizations. Prison control is the main flashpoint: earlier escapes of 20 Barrio 18 leaders from prison exposed the state's weakness, and transfers of gang leaders to tighter prisons provoke violent pushback.
year: On 17 January 2026 gang members rioted in Renovación I (Escuintla), Fraijanes II and Preventivo prisons, holding 46 people hostage to demand transfers of their leaders to lower-security prisons. Coordinated attacks in the capital and nearby towns killed eight police officers (later reported as 11) and injured ten. On 18 January President Arévalo declared a 30-day nationwide state of siege; police retook Renovación I with armoured vehicles and tear gas in about 15 minutes and freed all hostages. Killings of police continued through the year, reaching 20 by 27 July 2026.
situation: As of late October 2026 the army remains deployed in the streets and police remain targets; homicides showed a 'rebound' by mid-2026 according to local media, but no consolidated national figures were found.
technical: Prison riots, 17 to 18 Jan 2026: 46 hostages across three prisons; Renovación I retaken in about 15 minutes with armoured vehicles and tear gas; 9 guards freed there, 28 people at Fraijanes II and 9 at Preventivo (El País Cali/AFP).
State of siege: 30 days, nationwide, suspending rights of assembly and allowing detention without a court order; required congressional ratification.
Police deaths: 20 PNC officers killed on duty by 27 Jul 2026, against 10 in all of 2025; half attributed to gangs (Interior Minister Villeda via EFE).
Prison escapes: 20 Barrio 18 leaders had escaped prison before the riots; 6 were recaptured and 1 shot dead by mid-January (AFP).
Alleged Barrio 18 leader Aldo Dupie 'El Lobo' was presented in custody after the attacks; investigators link the police killings to retaliation for the state retaking the prisons (AFP; EFE).
Defence Minister Henry Sáenz said the army would stay in the streets under the state of siege (AFP).
casualties: At least 8 police killed on 17 to 18 Jan 2026 (AFP), later reported as 11 in the Jan to Feb attacks; 20 police killed by 27 Jul 2026 (EFE via El Nuevo Diario). National homicide totals for 2026 were not found.

timeline.event: Barrio 18 riots in three prisons and coordinated attacks kill at least 8 police.
President Arévalo declares a 30-day nationwide state of siege.
Police deaths in 2026 reach 20, double the 2025 total.

outlook: Watch prison transfers of gang leaders, which have triggered violence before, renewals of emergency measures, and whether Guatemala adopts harsher detention and emergency policies.

battles.name: Barrio 18 prison riots and attacks on police
battles.place: Renovación I prison (Escuintla), Fraijanes II and Preventivo prisons, and Guatemala City area, Guatemala
sides: Guatemalan police, army and prison authorities
battles.outcome: State retook all three prisons and freed 46 hostages; 30-day nationwide state of siege declared on 18 Jan 2026.
battles.forces: Police with armoured vehicles and tear gas retook Renovación I in about 15 minutes; army deployed in the streets.
battles.losses: At least 8 police killed and 10 injured (AFP); later reported as 11 police killed in the Jan to Feb attacks (EFE); 1 alleged gang member killed.
battles.significance: The most serious gang challenge to the Guatemalan state in years, prompting emergency rule.
